key_insight: A derivative-free, mesh-free neural solver can capture macroscopic turbulent flow behavior more accurately by modeling walker motion analytically to include directional stretching and reduce sampling noise.
engineering_relevance: This provides a non-intrusive multiscale option for turbulent flow simulation that avoids explicit derivatives and fine-grid resolution while still learning large-scale dynamics.
method: Replaces derivative-based PDE residuals with stochastic walkers in a neural network framework.
Uses an analytic local-motion approximation for walkers to capture swirl and directional stretching.
Eliminates random sampling noise in target evaluation to improve training stability and accuracy.
evidence_signal: On two two-dimensional turbulent flow cases, the method reproduced the macroscopic energy spectrum of fully resolved reference simulations more accurately than the standard DFLM, especially in regions of strong stretching.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on two 2D turbulent cases, so scalability to more complex 3D flows or broader turbulence regimes remains to be validated.
paper_title: A derivative-free framework for capturing macroscopic behavior of incompressible turbulent flows
